description: Wave coverage for Politics_satisfaction0 (satisfaction-frame items only) and Politics_attitude0 (broader positive/negative attitude family). For each variable: ATP waves that include it, the canonical wording, the response-option format, and the binarization rule. Use this to (a) pull gold-standard topline proportions for ∆̂_j across exchangeable historical tasks, and (b) extract demographics for LLM-conditioned simulation.
binarization_convention: For scaled items: 'positive' = options labeled Very/Extremely/Fairly/Mostly/Somewhat (satisfied | favorable | approve); 'negative' = options labeled Somewhat/Mostly/Not too/Not at all/Very (dissatisfied | unfavorable | disapprove). 'Not sure' / 'Have not heard enough' / DK / refused are dropped from the denominator (mirrors the SATIS no_answer convention in data/use_data/Politics_basic0/SATIS.csv).

SATIS.wording: All in all, are you satisfied or dissatisfied with the way things are going in this country today?

SATISFPERS.wording: Overall, are you satisfied or dissatisfied with the way things are going in YOUR LIFE today?
SATISFPERS.notes: Closest pure-binary analogue of SATIS — same response options, different referent.

REDIST_SATIS.wording: Are you satisfied or dissatisfied with how redistricting is being handled in your state?

CANDHOUSAT.wording: How satisfied are you with the choice of candidates for Congress in your district this November?

SATISPRESCAND.wording: What is your opinion of the presidential candidates for this year? Would you say that you are…

SATCAND_POST.wording: Now that the campaign is over, how satisfied were you with the choice of presidential candidates? Would you say that you were…

PRICANDSAT_R.wording: Now thinking about some of the candidates running for the Republican nomination for president… Regardless of who your first choice is, how would you feel if [CANDIDATE] became the Republican nominee in 2024?
PRICANDSAT_R.notes: Battery question — each named candidate yields its own ∆̂. Asked of Republicans/leaners only, so the underlying population differs from SATIS.

JOBSAT.wording: Overall, how satisfied are you with your job?
JOBSAT.notes: Use with caution — employment screening creates a different respondent pool than SATIS.

broader_attitude_family.description: Same positive/negative semantic frame as satisfaction items, but using approve/disapprove, favorable/unfavorable, or right-direction/wrong-track wording. Useful if you want the broader 'positive vs. negative attitude toward {target}' interpretation rather than strict satisfaction wording.

TRACK.wording: Do you think things in this country are generally going in the right direction or do you feel that things are off on the wrong track?

waves.notes: Phrasing: 'Generally headed in the right direction' vs. 'Off on the wrong track'.

TRACK.notes: Conceptually the closest 'cousin' to SATIS — same target (the country), positive/negative response, asked of all respondents. Treating SATIS and TRACK as exchangeable assumes question wording does not move the proportion meaningfully (a non-trivial assumption — Pew documents systematic gaps between satisfaction and direction framings).

POL1JB.wording: Do you approve or disapprove of the way Joe Biden is handling his job as president?

POL1DT.wording: Do you approve or disapprove of the way Donald Trump is handling his job as President?

INSTFAV_FED.wording: Do you have a favorable or unfavorable opinion of the federal government in Washington?
INSTFAV_FED.notes: Direct match to your example ('positive vs. negative attitude toward current government').

INSTFAV_STAT.wording: Do you have a favorable or unfavorable opinion of your STATE government?

INSTFAV_LOC.wording: Do you have a favorable or unfavorable opinion of your LOCAL government?

INSTFAV_CONG.wording: Do you have a favorable or unfavorable opinion of Congress?

INSTFAV_COURT.wording: Do you have a favorable or unfavorable opinion of the Supreme Court?

task_exchangeability_notes.rationale: Tier 1 items are the only ones with native two-option Satisfied/Dissatisfied responses, so they are most plausibly exchangeable in form with the running SATIS example. Tier 2 share the satisfied/dissatisfied semantic frame but require binarization, which adds a measurement-design difference into ∆̂_j. Tier 3 changes the underlying population (employment, party). Tier 4 abandons the satisfaction wording but preserves the binary positive/negative attitude frame — useful if you want to argue exchangeability at the level of 'positive-vs-negative attitude toward {target}' rather than 'satisfaction with {target}'. Note that within Tier 4, mixing referents (presidential approval, institutional favorability, country direction) introduces target heterogeneity that strict exchangeability may not survive; the principled move is to either (a) keep targets matched (e.g. only TRACK with SATIS, both about the country) or (b) condition demographics finely enough that target-level shifts are absorbed by group-level means.
